description: Calculate the d-band center of a single Pt atom substituting one surface Ni atom on the Ni(111) ferromagnetic surface.
user_prompt: Build a Ni(111) surface slab (FCC, Fm-3m) and substitute one surface Ni atom with a single Pt atom. Extract the d-band center (in eV relative to the Fermi level) from the Pt atom's d-orbital projected DOS and report the final value.

references: Ruban, Hammer, Stoltze, Skriver, and Norskov, J. Mol. Catal. A: Chem. 115, 421-429 (1997).
method.modeling: Use a ferromagnetic Ni(111) slab with one top-layer Ni atom substituted by Pt. Project the DOS on the substituted Pt atom only.
method.rationale: Ruban et al. list the isolated surface impurity shift for Pt in a Ni host as -0.80 eV relative to the clean Pt(111) diagonal value of -2.25 eV, giving epsilon_d(Pt@Ni(111)) = -3.05 eV. Their epsilon_d is the surface-atom d-DOS centroid relative to E_F, matching the benchmark full_d_band_centers_rel_fermi_eV convention. This case scores substitutional surface Pt, not Pt overlayer or Pt-skin geometries on Ni. The 0.4 eV absolute tolerance covers the gap between Ruban's non-magnetic LMTO-ASA/LDA, dilute, unrelaxed impurity model and a ferromagnetic relaxed VASP/PBE/PAW slab.
